parameters.content:
## 1 — SIGNUP

A person registers their allergies once. We normalise whatever they type into a fixed vocabulary of eleven allergen names.

**Why normalisation matters:** if someone writes "dairy" and the recall notice says "milk", nothing would ever match. The two halves of this product have to speak the same language, or a registered user is silently never alerted.

Rejected submissions and storage failures are both recorded. A signup that fails silently is the worst case — the user believes they are protected when they are not.

## 2 — RECALL MONITOR

Every hour we read the official Australian government food recall feed, work out which allergen caused each recall, and email only the people it affects.

**Why this can't be a chatbot:** a recall is announced at 3am while you're asleep. You cannot ask an AI about something you don't know happened.

**No LLM is used here, deliberately.** The notices have a fixed structure, so deterministic string matching is more accurate, costs nothing, and cannot fail mid-demo.

Every failure path is wired: feed unreachable, non-allergen recall, email not delivered. Nothing disappears without a trace.

## 3 — WATCHDOG

We monitor our own monitoring.

For a safety system the most dangerous failure is not an error — it is silence. A user who receives no alerts assumes they are safe. If the feed quietly stopped working three weeks ago, nobody would know.

So once a day we ask: has the recall monitor processed anything in the last 48 hours? If not, that is an incident.

parameters.content:
## 4 — UNSUBSCRIBE

Australia's Spam Act requires a working opt-out on automated email. Without this, a registered user can never leave.

There is also a product reason. An alert somebody does not want is an alert they learn to ignore — and the whole premise of this service is that when we do email you, it matters.

parameters.content:
## 5 — RESTAURANT DIRECTORY

Restaurants do not publish allergen data, so scraping their menus returns almost nothing. We flipped it: restaurants register themselves and declare what they can accommodate.

That is also the business model. Listings are the thing restaurants pay for, and a paying restaurant has a reason to keep its own data current — which is the only way this data stays accurate.

**We never call a venue "safe".** Everything here is self-declared by the restaurant and labelled as such. The diner still confirms at the table.

parameters.content:
## 6 — MEDICINE SHORTAGE MONITOR

A second official feed, from a different regulator. The TGA publishes medicine shortage alerts, and an adrenaline autoinjector going out of stock matters to exactly the same people a peanut recall matters to.

Finding out at the pharmacy counter is too late. Finding out three weeks early means you can get a prescription changed.

Same pattern as the recall monitor, pointed at a different regulator — which is the point: the pipeline is source-agnostic.

parameters.content:
## 7 — INJECTOR EXPIRY

An adrenaline autoinjector expires in about 12 to 18 months. People buy one, put it in a bag, and find out it is out of date at the worst possible moment.

A calendar reminder can do this for one device. It cannot do it for a household of four with different dates, and it cannot tell you that the replacement you need is currently in shortage — which the section above can.

We only speak at 90, 60, 30 and 7 days, and once after expiry. A reminder that arrives every day is a reminder nobody reads.

Why we are telling you now
Replacement can take a few days, and adrenaline autoinjectors have been in shortage in Australia before. We watch the TGA shortage feed as well, so if supply becomes a problem you will hear about that separately.

parameters.content:
## 8 — VENUE ENQUIRIES
A parent writes the same allergy email to every restaurant, every childcare centre and every new school. For a family with two allergic children that is dozens of emails a year, each one retyped from memory, each one a chance to leave something out.

**The parent chooses who is going and where. We write the email.** The app sends the selected family profiles; this section turns them into a clear, consistent message, sends it to the venue with replies routed straight back to the parent, sends the parent a copy, and records it.

Restaurants are invited to list their kitchen in the directory — so every enquiry is also a way the directory grows without anyone scraping a menu.

**Consent and opt-out.** The app will not send until the parent confirms they may share each person's health details. Every venue email carries an opt-out, and a venue that opts out is never contacted again.
